Welcome to Frant Church of England Primary School
On behalf of our school community, I would like to offer a warm welcome to Frant CE Primary School which lies at the heart of the vibrant, village community. Thank you for taking the time to visit our website to find out more about us. The shortcuts below will take you to the most useful sections for parents while the full site can be explored via the menu at the top.
Frant Church of England School is part of The Weald Federation of schools along with Mark Cross, Mayfield and Five Ashes. We work closely together to enhance both the academic and pastoral opportunities for the pupils.
Admissions Enquiries for Frant
Please contact the school office if you wish to book a viewing of the school for in-year admissions on 01892 750243

pageCache.pageTitle: Inclusion and SEND at Frant School – Frant Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Inclusion and SEND at Frant School
Frant CE Primary School is committed to removing barriers to achievement for children who may require additional provision and resources to support their learning and/ or emotional development.
We are an inclusive school and believe that all children, including those identified as having special educational needs and/or a disability, have a common entitlement to a broad, balanced academic and social curriculum.
The Special Educational Needs Code of Practice lies at the heart of our school’s SEND strategy and sets out the processes and procedures that all organisations should follow to meet the needs of children. The Code describes a graduated approach that recognises that children learn in different ways and can have different kinds of SEND.
Here at Frant, we have an Inclusion Team that is responsible, in consultation with class teachers, for identifying children with special needs and to then plan for the appropriate help and support. If necessary, help and advice will be sought from outside agencies. Very occasionally a statutory assessment will be made, leading to an Education, Health and Care Plan.
Our Inclusion Team is led by Jill Thomson and supported by Em Comeau and Joanna Challis (SENDCo).
Please contact the Inclusion Team at any time via the school office, frantoffice@thewealdfederation.org
This Special Educational Needs Information Report also acts as our SEND policy (below).

Attendance & Absence
Reporting Student Absences
If your child is too unwell to attend school, please inform the school office before 9:30 am with details of their absence.
Log Absences via the Arbor Parent App
You can report your child’s sickness directly through the Arbor Parent App. Using the app is a great help to our staff, and we appreciate your support in making use of this tool.
Other Ways to Report an Absence
You can also report absences by:
Please note: During busy times or early mornings, we may not be able to answer your call immediately. If this happens, please leave a voicemail message – we will listen to it and follow up if we need any further information.
All other absence requests should be submitted on either an appointment form or a withdrawal from learning form (see below).
Emailing the school office: frantoffice@thewealdfederation.org
Calling us on 01892 750243
The 48 Hour Rule
If your child has had a vomiting or diarrhoea bug they need to remain at home for 48 hours after the last bout of illness, as per NHS guidance.Add the is my child too ill for school link: www.nhs.uk/live-well/is-my-child-too-ill-for-school
Someone Else Picking Up?
If there is someone else collecting your child from school the class teacher needs to know. Please let the office know or the class teacher.

pageCache.pageTitle: Performance Data – Frant Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Performance Data
School Evaluation and Improvement
The Executive Headteacher and the Head of School regularly evaluate the school’s strengths and areas for development against the standards set out in each of the Ofsted areas. As a Church of England Primary School, we also consider our Christian Distinctiveness.
Please note that it is not possible to calculate KS1 to KS2 progress measures for the academic year 2024 to 2025. This is because there is no relevant KS1 data required to calculate KS1 to KS2 progress measures for this cohort, as primary tests and assessments were cancelled in the academic year 2020 to 2021 due to COVID-19 disruption.
Frant CEP School Outcomes for the Academic Year 2024 to 2025
Exp+ = scaled score of 100 or higherGDS = scaled score at or above higher threshold in tested subjects (teacher assessed as GDS for writing)SS = average (mean) scaled score across all pupils (pupils with no scaled score or N are discounted)RWM = the pupil must have achieved the stated level of performance in all 3 subjects – reading, writing and maths
Please note: When comparing data with other schools, please bear in mind that we are a small school with a maximum of 15 pupils per year group. Therefore, each child can represent at least 7% of the overall percentage of the cohort.
Early Years Foundation Stage
The Early Years Curriculum is a stand alone curriculum that the children follow in Reception, their first year in Primary School. At the end of Reception, they move on to the National Curriculum (Year 1 onwards). A ‘good level of development’ (GLD) shows that children have reached the expected level in the prime areas of learning (Personal, Social and Emotional Development; Communication and Language; Physical Development) along with specific aspects of mathematics and literacy.
Phonic Screening Check
We follow the Twinkl Phonics Scheme, which our children really enjoy. We ensure that each child’s decodable reading book matches their stage of phonic development so that they can practice applying their phonic knowledge independently to build confidence in their reading skills. We really appreciate the support that you give your child at home with their reading. Practice, little and often, makes a huge difference to a child’s success in the early stages of their reading development.
Year 6 SATS
At the end of Key Stage 2 (Year 6), children sit their national SATS tests in reading, grammar, punctuation and spelling and maths. Their writing is assessed by the class teacher using work that has been done throughout the year.

Admissions
Arrangements for School Admissions at 4+
The deadlines for the 2027-28 academic year admissions round are:

Closing date for appeals
Frant is a voluntary controlled school and the County Council makes arrangements for admissions at age 4+. You will find a detailed description of how to apply for a school place on the East Sussex website.
Please use the online Synergy Parent Portal to apply for a school place. If you require assistance, please contact admissions@eastsussex.gov.uk or 0300 330 9472. The closing date for primary school applications is 15th January 2027.
The admission limit for Frant is currently set at 15 as the number of children entering the Reception Year Group. If the School is over-subscribed, the authority uses a range of criteria to decide entry, including siblings already in the school and distance from home to school.
All children start full time in September, although there is usually a staggered start in the first few weeks to aid the children’s transition into school. Parents who are considering applying for places at Frant Primary School are invited to attend one of two New Parent Open sessions held in the Autumn Term.
Please consult our admissions policy Admissions Policy VC July 2026 for information on how places are allocated.
In Year Admissions
Applications can be made through East Sussex County Council website. If you are interested in a place at Frant CEP for your child, please telephone or email the school office and make an appointment to come and look around. We would be delighted to show you around the school in order that you can make a secure choice before applying for a place for your child.

Governors
Thank you for your interest in The Weald Federation and the work of the Governing Board. I am first and foremost a parent, so the interests of the existing and prospective children at our schools is my primary reason for being a governor. It is a pleasure and privilege to be Chair of Governors and to work with such a capable and committed team of governors, leaders and staff. I am recently retired, having spent nearly 33 years in a commercial, branded-sales environment, leading global teams and specialising in operations and data. I am committed to providing all our schools with the depth of experience and expertise that can only come from a stable, well-managed cooperative environment such as The Weald Federation, allowing them to maintain their distinctiveness, thrive and deliver the best possible outcomes for pupils, alongside the Christian ethos and values that are such a part of who we are.
Robert FrenchChair of Governors
Governors – Who We Are and What We Do
The Weald Federation’s full Governing Board meets a minimum of three times a year and each governor has one or more allocated roles, on the main committees (Education & Standards and Finance & Resources), specifically linking to one school or an important area such as Ethos. There are excellent training resources available across the full range of subject areas, and we also ensure that vital areas such as Safeguarding are fully understood by all.
The Governing Board has the ability to appoint people with specialist knowledge or commitment, so please get in touch if you are interested.
There are certain statutory requirements in terms of published information, so please see the documents below for more detail on the Governing Board and its activities.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum – Frant Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
Our curriculum is rooted in our Christian ethos and a deep sense of belonging, nurturing every child so they feel safe and valued in God’s love. Spirituality permeates all aspects of school life. It is the life‑giving nutrient system of our curriculum, helping every child grow in wisdom, compassion and purpose. Through our four curriculum branches we support children to develop strong and meaningful relationships with themselves, with others, with the wider world and with God.
We are proud that inclusion is deeply embedded in all we do. Like the bark of our curriculum tree, inclusion forms the protective, structural layer that surrounds, strengthens and holds together every aspect of teaching and learning. It reflects our belief that every child is uniquely valued by God and deserves equitable opportunities to thrive. We provide a rich, knowledge‑informed and experience‑led education that celebrates our community, broadens horizons and develops independence, curiosity and resilience. Uniquely and deliberately designed for our federation, our curriculum equips children to flourish as kind, confident and well‑rounded individuals who contribute positively to an ever‑changing and diverse world.

pageCache.text:
Collective Worship
Through our Christian ethos, high quality teaching and shared learning, we encourage everyone to discover who they are in relation to God, the World and one another. Our three guiding values—Respect, Compassion and Perseverance—shape this journey.
Alongside these, we explore 12 Christian Values in Collective Worship over a two-year cycle—one each term—to help children prepare for and positively contribute to our ever-changing and diverse world. Our daily Collective Worship is inclusive and invitational, rooted in our vision, exploring the life and teachings of Jesus. These 12 values, together with our spiritual practices, shape our pupils to prepare for, and positively contribute to, our ever-changing and diverse world.

Healthy Eating & School Meals
We are proud to work with Chartwells for your children’s school dinners.
Chartwells believe that the key to fuelling young minds comes from understanding both what they need and what they enjoy, which is why they develop nutritious and delicious food that pupils love, alongside helping to ensure a healthy body and mind. Their passionate culinary experts work closely with us to ensure every child receives healthy food, perfectly suited to meet their needs and dietary requirements.
The current meal price is £2.95
Click here to view menu
For children with food intolerances and allergies, Chartwells have a dedicated team of medical diet nutritionists on hand to support allergen aware children and their parents. More information on their medical diet process can be found here: The Chartwells Approach to Medical Diets | Chartwells
Parents and guardians can contact the medical diet nutrition team directly on: chartwells.medicaldiets@compass-group.co.uk.
To find out more about Chartwells, visit their Love School Meals website or contact the school catering team. Weblink: Love School Meals Website
